gate1_third_model_family.summary: 0/3 non-OLMo families replicate the MMLU letter-interface failure. Llama-2-7B letter 0.4100 (+14.11pp vs always-D 0.2689), Llama-3-8B 0.6220 (+35.31pp), Qwen3-8B-Base 0.7464 (+47.75pp). All n=14042, 0 nan. On Llama-3 and Qwen3 the letter interface is 16-23pp BETTER than content, inverting the 'content is the valid interface' narrative.
gate1_third_model_family.side_finding: Llama-2-7B has a 15.79% exact-tie rate and is nonetheless HEALTHY (+14.11pp, letter indistinguishable from content p=0.51), while OLMo-2 base has 0.13% ties and is also healthy. Tie rate does NOT order the pathology across families -> 'exact ties cause interface failure' is FALSIFIED as a family-general mechanism. Within OLMo-2 the tie rate still tracks damage (0.13 -> 24.36 -> 30.64%).

gate2_second_mc_benchmark.summary: On non-MMLU MC the interface/floor failure DOES reproduce. BoolQ's construct-appropriate null is 0.6217 (always-B), not 0.5: keep12/keep10/keep8 all sit BELOW it on the raw-LL interface and keep14 is n.s. (p=0.20) -> 4/6 arms indistinguishable from a constant predictor while their nominal 0.59-0.64 look 'passing' against a 0.50 chance line. OpenBookQA: longest-option null 0.3635 vs chance 0.2500; keep10 acc_norm 0.3560 is below that floor, and 3/15 arm-pair sign flips between acc and acc_norm. Residual fraction for base OBQA drops 45.9% -> 21.3% under the correct null (2.15x inflation from using chance).
gate2_second_mc_benchmark.caveat: The two interfaces used here are raw sum-LL vs length-normalised acc_norm, NOT MMLU's letter-vs-content. Report that difference explicitly; it is an analogous but not identical interface contrast.
gate2_second_mc_benchmark.negative_control: winogrande is structurally degenerate (both options share the continuation -> identical norm_lens, acc == acc_norm exactly, 100% tie rate). Cannot serve as an interface case; report as a control, not evidence.
gate2_second_mc_benchmark.clean_cases: CommonsenseQA (5-way) and SocialIQA (3-way): all 6 arms significantly ABOVE their constant-letter nulls on both interfaces -- the 'not everything collapses' side of the protocol.

gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.verdict: base arm DONE; keep8 arm running on .73
gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.base_arm_result: fp32 removes ALL exact ties (18 -> 0) but letter acc is UNCHANGED: 0.6054 both dtypes, delta +0.0000 CI95 [-0.0011,+0.0011], McNemar p=1.000. 96 letter argmax flips (0.68%), of which only 12 were the bf16-tied items. So on the intact model, ties are a bf16 artifact AND removing them changes nothing measurable.
gate3_fp32_causal_tie_test.note: gate-1's Llama-2 result (15.79% ties, fully healthy) now serves as an external positive control for 'ties without failure', which reframes what the keep8 arm can show.
